subject.title: fix(telegram): bound miniapp auth rate-limit map with sweep and cap

question: Should the Telegram Mini App auth route intentionally use a 1,024-key least-recently-used cap that may reset the stalest live IP’s window under sustained high-cardinality traffic?
rationale: The patch fixes unbounded process-lifetime state, but choosing eviction rather than fail-closed rejection defines the authentication endpoint’s overload security behavior.

options.title: Accept bounded LRU eviction
options.body: Accept the 1,024-key recency-preserving cap as the bounded-memory tradeoff, retaining the proposed tests and live proof.

options.title: Require a stricter overload policy
options.body: Specify and implement a different behavior when the live-key cap is reached, such as rejecting new keys rather than resetting a stale window.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded LRU eviction
recommendation.body: Accept the 1,024-key recency-preserving cap as the bounded-memory tradeoff, retaining the proposed tests and live proof.
